meaning: A breaker that stops calls to a failing dependency to prevent error propagation
definition: Tracks the error/timeout rate; once a threshold is exceeded it fails fast for a period instead of continuing to call a dying dependency.

meaning: A probing state that lets a few requests through after the open period
definition: After the wait duration the breaker allows N trial requests; success moves it to CLOSED, failure sends it back to OPEN.

meaning: Isolates resources (thread pools, connections) per dependency
definition: Limits concurrency per dependency so one slow dependency cannot consume all of the service's resources.

meaning: A chain reaction of failures spreading from one service to the whole system
definition: A slow dependency makes callers hold threads/connections, callers run out of resources and keep dragging their upstreams down.

meaning: A design pattern that stores the event in the DB in the local transaction before pushing it to the Message Broker
definition: Solves the Dual-Write problem between the Database and the Message Broker without Two-Phase Commit (2PC).

meaning: The problem of writing to two systems that share no transaction
definition: Writing to the Database and then publishing to the Broker (or vice versa) can half-succeed on a crash, causing lost or inconsistent data.

meaning: Capture data changes directly from the Database transaction log
definition: Reads the WAL/binlog (for example Debezium) to emit an event for every change, with no table polling.

meaning: A consumer that gives the same result when it processes the same message several times
definition: Required when delivery is at-least-once; typically uses a processed_message_id table or an upsert by business key.

meaning: Choose consistency or availability during a network partition
definition: Partitions are not optional; CAP only describes behavior during a partition and the C here is linearizability.

meaning: Extends CAP with the latency trade-off during normal operation
definition: Even without a partition you must choose between latency and consistency.

meaning: The two ends of the consistency model spectrum
definition: Linearizability behaves like a single copy; eventual only guarantees eventual convergence.

meaning: The condition that guarantees reads see the latest write
definition: With N replicas, if R plus W is greater than N the read set always intersects the write set.

meaning: Users see the data they just wrote
definition: A per-session guarantee, usually achieved by reading from the leader or using sticky sessions after a write.

meaning: Empirical verification of a distributed DB's consistency
definition: Jepsen analyses show whether a system keeps its promises under failures.

meaning: Load balancing at the transport or the application layer
definition: L4 forwards TCP/UDP very quickly; L7 understands HTTP to route by path, host and headers.

meaning: Algorithms for choosing a backend
definition: Round robin, weighted, least connections, least response time and consistent hashing.

meaning: Distinguishing alive from ready to serve
definition: Liveness reports the process is running; readiness reports it can take traffic; checks that are too shallow or too deep both carry risk.

meaning: A proxy in front of backends that accepts connections on their behalf
definition: Nginx, HAProxy, Envoy handle TLS, compression, caching and routing.

meaning: Pin a client to one backend
definition: Convenient for local sessions but prevents even load balancing and scaling; prefer stateless.

meaning: Send users to the nearest Region
definition: Global load balancing at the DNS layer or via anycast routing.

meaning: Two broker models
definition: A queue deletes a message after the ack and gives it to one consumer; a log keeps messages, supports many consumer groups and can replay.

meaning: Message delivery semantics
definition: Exactly-once is in practice at-least-once plus idempotent processing.

meaning: Where messages that failed many times go
definition: Prevents a poison message from crashing the consumer in a loop; alert when the DLQ has data.

meaning: Balancing ordering and parallelism
definition: Ordering is only guaranteed within a partition; each partition is assigned to one consumer in the group.

meaning: Handling consumers that are slower than producers
definition: Bound the queue, scale consumers or slow producers so the system does not overflow.

meaning: Several workers sharing work from one queue
definition: Raises throughput by adding workers; global ordering is no longer guaranteed.

meaning: A hash ring so adding or removing a node moves only about 1/N of the keys
definition: Nodes and keys sit on the same ring; a key goes clockwise to the first node; vnodes balance the load.

meaning: Pick the node with the largest hash(key, node)
definition: Simple, evenly distributed and needs no stored ring.

meaning: A consistent hashing algorithm that needs no stored ring
definition: Only numbers nodes sequentially, uses almost no memory, but does not support removing an arbitrary node.

meaning: Splits 16,384 slots across nodes
definition: Each key belongs to a slot; slots are moved between nodes to rebalance.

meaning: Changing the node count moves most keys
definition: With hash(key) mod N, adding or removing a node moves about (N-1)/N of the keys.

meaning: A common data copying model
definition: Single-leader writes go through the leader and are copied to followers synchronously, asynchronously or semi-synchronously; multi-leader and leaderless setups must resolve write conflicts.

meaning: Anomalies when reading from a lagging replica
definition: Not seeing data you just wrote, reads going back in time; mitigate by reading the leader after a write or using a sticky replica.

meaning: Range, hash, directory and how to choose a shard key
definition: The shard key needs high cardinality, even distribution and to match the access pattern so a request touches only one shard.

meaning: One shard overloaded by skewed distribution
definition: A monotonically increasing key or a celebrity key funnels all writes into one shard.

meaning: Two leaders coexisting and how to prevent it
definition: Automatic failover without fencing can create two leaders accepting writes and break consistency.

meaning: Two popular rate limiting algorithms
definition: A token bucket allows a burst up to the bucket capacity and then keeps the refill rate; a leaky bucket smooths output at a fixed rate.

meaning: A memory-efficient sliding window approximation
definition: Combines the current and previous windows by proportion; avoids the double burst of a fixed window.

meaning: Distributed limiting using atomic operations
definition: Uses INCR with EXPIRE or a Lua script to check and deduct atomically across many instances.

meaning: How to tell clients they exceeded the quota
definition: Return 429 with Retry-After and quota headers; clients should back off and respect the wait time.

meaning: Protecting the system versus fairness between clients
definition: Rate limiting divides quota per client; load shedding drops requests when the system is truly overloaded.

meaning: Behavior when a protection component fails
definition: Fail-open lets traffic through to stay available; fail-closed blocks to stay safe; the choice must be deliberate.

meaning: Cache read/write strategies
definition: Cache-aside has the application populate on a miss; write-through writes both synchronously; write-behind writes asynchronously, which is fast but can lose data.

meaning: TTL, explicit delete, event-driven
definition: Usually combines a TTL as a safety net with deleting the key on write.

meaning: Eviction policies when the cache is full
definition: LRU drops the least recently used item; LFU drops the least frequently used item.

meaning: Two classic cache failures
definition: Penetration is a non-existent key that always misses; avalanche is many keys expiring at once.

meaning: A measure of cache effectiveness
definition: Hits over total accesses; a low ratio shows the key design or TTL is a poor fit.

meaning: Many requests miss the cache together and hit the Database at once
definition: Also called Thundering Herd / Dog-piling: one hot key expires and thousands of requests recompute the value together.

meaning: Randomly refresh the cache early before the TTL expires
definition: Each request decides to recompute with a probability that grows as the TTL nears its end, spreading out the refresh time.

meaning: A distributed lock so only one process recomputes the cache
definition: Uses Redis SET key value NX PX ttl; only the lock holder rebuilds the cache while other requests wait or return stale data.

meaning: Merge requests for the same key into one backend call
definition: Within a process the first request executes and requests for the same key wait and share the result.

meaning: Add a random offset to the TTL
definition: Prevents many keys that were set together from expiring together (mass expiration).

meaning: Two storage engine families and their read/write trade-offs
definition: B-Tree updates in place and is good for reads and range scans; LSM writes sequentially then compacts in the background and is good for heavy writes.

meaning: I/O amplification in a storage engine
definition: The real I/O is larger than the original data; each engine trades off between writes, reads and space.

meaning: The rule for using a multi-column index
definition: An index (a, b) supports filtering by a, or a and b, but is not efficient when filtering by b alone.

meaning: An index that holds enough columns to avoid reading the table
definition: The query gets its data straight from the index, greatly reducing I/O.

meaning: Reading the query execution plan
definition: Shows whether the planner uses an index and the actual time of each step.

meaning: A probabilistic structure that helps skip data that does not contain a key
definition: Returns "definitely not present" or "possibly present"; used in LSMs and to prevent cache penetration.

meaning: The four properties of a transaction
definition: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability; Durability is achieved through the write-ahead log.

meaning: Dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom, write skew
definition: The higher the isolation level, the fewer the anomalies but the more waiting or aborting.

meaning: Snapshot reads that do not block writers
definition: Each transaction sees a consistent snapshot; write skew is still possible.

meaning: Two anomalies that are often confused
definition: A lost update is two read-modify-writes overwriting each other on the same row; write skew is two transactions writing different rows but violating a shared constraint.

meaning: Two ways to handle write contention
definition: Lock the row as soon as you read it, or use a version column and check the number of rows affected on update.

meaning: The DB kills one transaction and the application must retry
definition: Reduce deadlocks with a consistent table/row access order and short transactions.

meaning: Conventions for naming, methods and status codes
definition: Resources are nouns, methods have correct semantics, status codes are accurate and errors are consistent.

meaning: Stable pagination for large tables
definition: Offset is slow and drifts when data changes; cursor/keyset is fast and stable.

meaning: Evolving an API without breaking clients
definition: Prefer backward-compatible changes such as adding fields; have a deprecation policy.

meaning: A standard for describing errors in HTTP APIs
definition: A consistent error structure with type, title and detail so clients can handle it by machine.

meaning: Choosing an API style by need
definition: REST is easy to cache and public; gRPC is fast for service-to-service; GraphQL is flexible to query but hard to cache.

meaning: A machine-readable description of the API contract
definition: Used to generate documentation, client SDKs and contract tests.

meaning: The standard authorization flow for SPAs and mobile
definition: The client exchanges the authorization code for a token along with the code_verifier to prevent code interception.

meaning: The identity layer built on OAuth 2.0
definition: The ID token says who signed in; the access token is used to call APIs.

meaning: What you must check when receiving a token
definition: Verify the signature, whitelist algorithms, check expiry, issuer and audience; the payload is not secret.

meaning: Protecting sessions and preventing CSRF
definition: HttpOnly cookies stop JavaScript from reading them; SameSite and CSRF tokens reduce request forgery attacks.

meaning: Two authorization models
definition: RBAC is by role; ABAC is by attributes and context, more flexible but more complex.

meaning: A missing per-object permission check
definition: Changing an ID in the URL to reach other people's data; you need an ownership check on every object.

meaning: A unique key so retries do not repeat side effects
definition: The client sends a key; the server stores the key with the result under a unique constraint and returns the old result when it sees it again.

meaning: Spaced retries with randomness
definition: Increase the wait progressively and add jitter so that not every client retries at once.

meaning: Multi-layer retries overloading a dependency
definition: Three layers each trying three times multiply into 27 requests; retry at one layer and with a limit.

meaning: Removing duplicate messages on the consumer side
definition: Store the processed messageId in the same transaction as the side effect, or use an upsert by business key.

meaning: Two quick performance review frameworks
definition: RED: Rate, Errors, Duration for services; USE: Utilization, Saturation, Errors for resources.

meaning: Visualizing the functions that cost CPU
definition: Shows how much CPU time each call stack takes so you can find the bottleneck.

meaning: Choosing the connection pool size
definition: A pool that is too small makes requests wait and one that is too large overloads the DB; start small, then measure and adjust.

meaning: One query for the list plus one query per element
definition: The number of queries grows linearly with the list size; fix with a JOIN or prefetch.

meaning: A measurement bias when load testing latency
definition: A tool that waits for a response before sending the next underestimates tail latency.

meaning: Blocked threads lengthen the queue
definition: Every thread waits on slow I/O so new requests have no thread to run on even though the CPU is idle.

meaning: Comparing estimates with reality
definition: Estimated row counts far from the real ones are usually caused by stale statistics.

meaning: Three join algorithms
definition: Nested loop suits few rows with an index; hash join suits large tables with equality conditions; merge join suits already sorted input.

meaning: Conditions that allow index use
definition: Wrapping a function around a column or a LIKE starting with a wildcard defeats the index.

meaning: Fast and stable pagination
definition: Keyset uses a condition on the sort key; a large OFFSET scans and discards many rows.

meaning: Per-group computation without a self-join
definition: ROW_NUMBER, LAG, SUM OVER for top-N per group and running totals.

meaning: A common ORM performance trap
definition: One query for the list and then one query per element when a lazy relation is accessed.

meaning: Loading relations deliberately
definition: JOIN FETCH or selectinload collapses many queries into a few.

meaning: Fetch only the needed columns for read queries
definition: Avoid loading a whole entity graph when only a few columns are needed.

meaning: How an ORM tracks changes
definition: The ORM detects modified entities and flushes on commit; the same entity within a context is the same object.

meaning: Versioned schema change management
definition: Do not let the ORM update the schema on production by itself.

meaning: A two-way channel and one-way push
definition: SSE is simple over HTTP with auto-reconnect; WebSocket is full-duplex for chat and collaboration.

meaning: Two ways to fake real time over HTTP
definition: Long polling holds the request open until data arrives, reducing latency compared with repeated asking.

meaning: Scaling persistent connections across nodes
definition: A connection is tied to one node, so pub/sub or a registry is needed to deliver messages to users on other nodes.

meaning: Keeping and restoring persistent connections
definition: Periodic ping/pong against timeouts and reconnecting with jitter.

meaning: Mass reconnection causing overload
definition: After an incident many clients reconnect at once; jitter and a rate limit on accepted connections are needed.

meaning: The four NoSQL models
definition: Each model optimizes one access pattern.

meaning: Design by access pattern
definition: Several entities in one table.

meaning: The wide-column keys
definition: The partition decides the node; clustering sorts within the partition.

meaning: The document model
definition: Embed data that is read together.

meaning: Eventual consistency
definition: R + W > N for the latest read.

meaning: The inverted index
definition: A term points to the list of documents.

meaning: Ranking by relevance
definition: An improved TF-IDF.

meaning: Sharding and replicas
definition: The number of primary shards is hard to change.

meaning: Deep pagination
definition: Replaces a large from+size.

meaning: Two field types
definition: Text is analyzed, keyword is verbatim.

meaning: Comparing architecture styles and when to move
definition: Microservices trade in-code complexity for distributed-system complexity; a modular monolith is a sensible starting point.

meaning: A business boundary for splitting services
definition: Each context has its own model and language; boundaries follow business capabilities rather than technical layers.

meaning: Each service owns its own data
definition: Never read another service's DB directly; exchange data through APIs or events.

meaning: Gradually replace a legacy system with new services
definition: Wrap and move one feature at a time to new services until the legacy system can be retired.

meaning: Split into services but still tightly dependent
definition: Sharing a DB or needing to deploy together: you pay microservices' costs without their benefits.

meaning: Architecture mirrors the organization's structure
definition: System design resembles how teams communicate; split teams by business capability.

meaning: Communicating through events via a broker
definition: A producer emits what has happened and consumers react on their own, reducing coupling but making debugging harder.

meaning: Two ways to carry data in an event
definition: A notification only signals a change; state transfer includes enough data so the consumer does not need to call back.

meaning: Self-organizing or coordinated
definition: Choreography relies on events between services; orchestration has a coordinator commanding each step.

meaning: Managing event schema evolution
definition: Checks backward and forward compatibility so schema changes do not break consumers.

meaning: A standard for describing events across systems
definition: A common format for event metadata across many platforms.

meaning: A distributed transaction as a chain of local transactions plus compensation
definition: Achieves atomicity at the business level without a global lock like 2PC.

meaning: Semantically undoing completed steps
definition: Not a rollback: for example a refund or a correction email; it must be idempotent and retryable.

meaning: The trade-off between a global lock and eventual consistency
definition: 2PC gives strong consistency but blocks and is hard to scale; a saga is flexible but lacks isolation.

meaning: Handling the lack of isolation in a saga
definition: Semantic lock, commutative updates, pessimistic view and re-read value.

meaning: A platform for durable workflow orchestration
definition: Stores workflow state so it can resume after failures; suits multi-step sagas.

meaning: Three kinds of signals for observing a system
definition: Metrics show that there is a problem, traces show where, and logs explain why.

meaning: An open standard for collecting telemetry
definition: A common API, SDK and Collector for logs, metrics and traces, independent of the vendor.

meaning: Propagating context across services
definition: A trace consists of many spans; the trace-id is propagated via the traceparent header, including through message queues.

meaning: Measuring reliability against targets
definition: The SLI is the indicator, the SLO the target, and the error budget the allowed deviation that balances feature velocity and stability.

meaning: Keeping error or slow traces when sampling
definition: The decision is made after the trace completes, so rare but important traces are kept.

meaning: The risk of cost explosion from detailed labels
definition: Putting user_id or request_id into metric labels makes the number of time series explode.

meaning: A leader-based consensus algorithm
definition: The leader accepts writes and commits only once a majority of nodes have stored them; the foundation of etcd, Consul and KRaft.

meaning: Electing a leader by term
definition: A follower whose random election timeout expires becomes a candidate; with a majority of votes it becomes the leader.

meaning: The same log in the same order gives the same state
definition: Every node applies the same sequence of commands so they reach the same state.

meaning: How many nodes are needed to tolerate f failures
definition: A cluster of 2f+1 nodes tolerates f failed nodes; 3 nodes tolerate 1, 5 nodes tolerate 2.

meaning: Comparing two consensus algorithms
definition: Equivalent in safety, but Raft was designed to be easier to understand and implement.

meaning: Coordination systems built on consensus
definition: Used for configuration, leader election and distributed locks, not for storing large data.

meaning: Control plane and node components
definition: API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager; kubelet and the container runtime on the node.

meaning: The relationship between workload objects
definition: A Pod is the smallest unit; a Deployment manages ReplicaSets for rolling updates and rollbacks.

meaning: How to expose services inside and outside the cluster
definition: A Service gives stable internal L4 load balancing; an Ingress routes external HTTP L7 traffic in.

meaning: Kubernetes' three kinds of probes
definition: Liveness restarts when hung, readiness decides whether to take traffic, startup protects slow-starting applications.

meaning: Resources, scheduling and the consequences of exceeding them
definition: Requests are used for scheduling; exceeding the CPU limit is throttled, exceeding the memory limit is OOMKilled.

meaning: Automatically scaling the number of Pods with load
definition: Adjusts the replica count based on CPU or a custom metric.

meaning: North-south and east-west traffic
definition: The gateway handles external clients coming into the system; the mesh handles communication between internal services.

meaning: A proxy beside each service acting as the data plane
definition: Handles mTLS, retries, timeouts and telemetry without changing application code.

meaning: Popular service meshes
definition: The control plane configures the proxies and issues certificates for the whole mesh.

meaning: Both sides authenticate with certificates
definition: Used for zero trust between services: both client and server prove their identity.

meaning: Gradually shift traffic to the new version
definition: For example 5%, then 25%, then 100% until the new version is trusted.

meaning: A dedicated gateway for each client type
definition: Each client type gets its own optimized backend layer instead of one shared API.

meaning: Separate the write model from the read model
definition: A command changes state through an aggregate; a query reads from a denormalized, eventually consistent read model.

meaning: Store the sequence of events as the source of truth
definition: State is the fold of events; snapshots avoid replaying from the beginning.

meaning: Rebuild the read model from events
definition: A projection reads events and updates the read model, and can replay everything to rebuild it.

meaning: Evolving the schema of immutable events
definition: Converts old events to the new form on read instead of editing stored events.

meaning: Handling concurrent writes to an aggregate
definition: Write events with the expected version; on a version mismatch, reject or retry.

meaning: Deleting personal data when events are immutable
definition: Encrypt personal data and delete the key to make the data unreadable.

meaning: How AWS decides Allow/Deny when there are many policies
definition: Implicit deny by default; an explicit Deny in any policy (identity, resource, SCP, boundary) always beats every Allow.

meaning: Grant only the minimum permissions needed to work
definition: Start from the smallest permissions and expand as needed; use IAM Access Analyzer to generate policies from actual activity.

meaning: Policies managed by AWS versus self-written ones
definition: AWS managed policies are created and updated by AWS, convenient but often broad; customer managed policies are written by you, reusable and versioned.

meaning: A temporary identity that issues short-lived credentials
definition: A role is assumed through STS to obtain temporary credentials for EC2, Lambda, cross-account access and federation, replacing long-term access keys.

meaning: Sign in to AWS with an IdP such as Google or a corporate AD
definition: Connects an IdP through SAML 2.0/OIDC so users get SSO into many accounts without separate IAM users.

meaning: Enable multi-factor authentication for the root account
definition: Root has full access and is not restricted by IAM policies: enable MFA, delete access keys and use it only for mandatory tasks.

meaning: A resource-based policy for the whole bucket
definition: A JSON policy attached to the bucket to allow/deny by principal, IP, VPC endpoint, HTTPS or encryption header.

meaning: The mechanism that disables ACLs so the bucket owner owns every object
definition: New buckets default to Bucket owner enforced: ACLs are disabled and permissions are managed only through policies; ACLs are the legacy bucket/object-level mechanism.

meaning: A breaker that blocks any configuration that makes a bucket public
definition: On by default for new buckets, it overrides any bucket policy/ACL that grants public access; it can also be set at the account level.

meaning: S3's three kinds of server-side encryption
definition: SSE-S3 has S3 manage the key (the default); SSE-KMS uses a KMS key with auditing and permissions; SSE-C has the customer send the key with every request.

meaning: A policy condition that enforces HTTPS
definition: A bucket policy denies every request with aws:SecureTransport = false to guarantee encryption in transit.

meaning: A limit on KMS requests per second per Region
definition: SSE-KMS calls KMS for every upload/download so it can be throttled; reduce it with S3 Bucket Key.

meaning: Keep every version of an object in a bucket
definition: Three states Unversioned/Enabled/Suspended; once enabled it can only be Suspended, not fully disabled; every write creates a new versionId.

meaning: A "soft delete" marker in a versioned bucket
definition: A DELETE without a versionId only inserts a delete marker; remove the marker to restore the object.

meaning: Require MFA to permanently delete versions
definition: Requires the root user's MFA to permanently delete object versions or change the versioning state.

meaning: Asynchronously copy objects to another bucket
definition: CRR/SRR require versioning on both buckets and an IAM role; only new objects are replicated after the rule is created.

meaning: Replicate objects that existed before the rule was created
definition: Uses S3 Batch Operations to copy existing objects or objects that previously failed to replicate.

meaning: Storage classes trading storage price against retrieval price
definition: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant/Flexible/Deep Archive differ in price, latency, retrieval fee and AZ count.

meaning: Automatic tiering by access level
definition: No retrieval fee but a per-object monitoring fee; suits data with unpredictable access patterns.

meaning: Restore speeds for data in Glacier
definition: Flexible: Expedited 1–5 minutes, Standard 3–5 hours, Bulk 5–12 hours; Deep Archive: Standard ≤ 12 hours, Bulk ≤ 48 hours.

meaning: Rules that automatically transition or delete objects by age
definition: Consists of Transition actions (change storage class) and Expiration actions (delete objects, noncurrent versions, incomplete multipart uploads).

meaning: The minimum storage time that is still billed
definition: IA 30 days, Glacier Instant/Flexible 90 days, Deep Archive 180 days; deleting or transitioning early is still billed in full.

meaning: S3's request limit per prefix
definition: Each prefix supports at least 3,500 PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE and 5,500 GET/HEAD per second; raise throughput with more prefixes.

meaning: Upload a large object as many parallel parts
definition: Recommended for files > 100 MB, required for > 5 GB; parts of 5 MB–5 GB, at most 10,000 parts, objects up to 5 TB.

meaning: Download several chunks of one object in parallel
definition: A GET with the Range header to speed up downloads or read only part of an object.

meaning: Speed up uploads through CloudFront edge locations
definition: The client uploads to the nearest edge and then travels over the AWS backbone to the bucket; it costs extra.

meaning: Pay per second/hour with no commitment
definition: Linux/Windows are billed per second (60-second minimum); the most flexible but the most expensive among shared-tenancy options.

meaning: A 1- or 3-year commitment for a discount
definition: Up to 72% off; Standard RI gives a bigger discount, Convertible RI can change the instance family; pay All/Partial/No Upfront.

meaning: Commit to $/hour spend for 1–3 years
definition: Up to 72% off, more flexible than RI; Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2, Fargate and Lambda.

meaning: Use spare capacity at up to 90% off
definition: AWS can reclaim it with a 2-minute warning; suits stateless, interruption-tolerant workloads.

meaning: Rent a whole physical server
definition: Exposes sockets/cores for per-core BYOL licenses and compliance; the highest cost.

meaning: A stateful virtual firewall attached to an instance's ENI
definition: Only Allow rules; inbound blocks everything by default, outbound allows everything by default; responses are passed automatically.

meaning: Comparing instance-level and subnet-level firewalls
definition: An SG is stateful, Allow-only, instance-level; a NACL is stateless, has Allow/Deny, subnet-level, with rules evaluated by number.

meaning: EC2's virtual network card
definition: Has its own private IP, MAC and Security Groups; attach extra ones to separate management/log networks or move to another instance on failover.

meaning: High-speed networking for EC2 using SR-IOV
definition: The Elastic Network Adapter gives bandwidth up to 100 Gbps, high PPS and low latency at no extra cost.

meaning: A network card for HPC and machine learning
definition: ENA plus OS-bypass (libfabric/MPI) for ultra-low-latency communication between nodes.

meaning: Pack instances close together in one AZ
definition: Low latency and high throughput for HPC; in exchange, a concentrated hardware failure risk.

meaning: Each instance on its own rack
definition: Maximum failure isolation, limited to 7 running instances per AZ per group, and can span several AZs.

meaning: Divide instances into independent rack groups
definition: At most 7 partitions per AZ; different partitions share no hardware; suits HDFS, HBase, Cassandra, Kafka.

meaning: The CLI command to move an instance to another placement group
definition: The instance must be stopped; it can only be done through the AWS CLI/SDK, not the console.

meaning: Public/private subnets are decided by the route table
definition: A subnet is public when its route table has 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to an Internet Gateway; each subnet is in exactly one AZ and AWS reserves 5 IPs per subnet.

meaning: Lets a private subnet go out to the Internet but not be reached
definition: Placed in a public subnet; you need one NAT Gateway per AZ for fault tolerance; IPv6 uses an Egress-only Internet Gateway.

meaning: Access AWS services without the Internet
definition: A Gateway endpoint is only for S3 and DynamoDB and is free; an Interface endpoint (PrivateLink) uses ENIs, is billed, and supports most other services.

meaning: A private connection between two VPCs
definition: A 1-to-1 relationship, non-transitive, and the two VPCs must not have overlapping CIDRs; it can be cross-Region and cross-account.

meaning: A central hub connecting many VPCs and on-premises
definition: A hub-and-spoke model with transitive routing, replacing a complex Peering mesh.

meaning: Choose a load balancer by layer 7, 4 or 3
definition: ALB (L7) routes by path/host; NLB (L4) has ultra-high performance and static IPs; GWLB (L3) inserts third-party appliances into the traffic path via GENEVE.

meaning: Distribute traffic evenly across targets in every AZ
definition: On by default for ALB, off for NLB/GWLB; enabling it on an NLB incurs inter-AZ traffic charges.

meaning: A policy that keeps a metric at a target value
definition: For example keep CPU at 50% — the ASG scales the instance count itself; simpler than Step/Simple scaling based on alarm thresholds.

meaning: Wait for in-flight requests to finish before removing a target
definition: Default 300 seconds on an ELB target group, avoiding cutting connections when an instance is replaced or scaled in.

meaning: Insert actions when an instance launches or terminates
definition: Lets you run setup scripts or save logs before an instance enters service or is destroyed.

meaning: Multi-AZ for fault tolerance, Read Replica for read scaling
definition: Multi-AZ uses a synchronous standby and automatic failover; a Read Replica replicates asynchronously, can be cross-Region and promoted to a standalone DB.

meaning: A shared volume with 6 copies across 3 AZs
definition: One writer and up to 15 readers share storage that grows to 128 TiB; failover is typically under ~30 seconds.

meaning: Aurora with ultra-low-latency cross-Region replication
definition: About 1 second of replication, cross-Region failover in about a minute; suits DR with a very small RPO.

meaning: A connection pool for RDS/Aurora
definition: Reduces failover time, protects the DB from connection storms (especially from Lambda) and supports IAM auth and Secrets Manager.

meaning: Aurora that scales automatically in ACU units
definition: Suits erratic load and dev/test; capacity changes continuously without dropping connections.

meaning: Choose an evenly distributed partition key to avoid hot partitions
definition: A high-cardinality key spreads load; a skewed key causes throttling even when total capacity remains.

meaning: DynamoDB's read and write capacity units
definition: 1 RCU = one strongly consistent read of ≤ 4 KB/second (eventually consistent gets twice as many); 1 WCU = one write of ≤ 1 KB/second; transactions cost double.

meaning: DynamoDB's two secondary index types
definition: A GSI changes the partition key, can be created at any time, and reads are eventually consistent; an LSI keeps the same partition key, is created only at table creation, at most 5.

meaning: A write-through in-memory cache for DynamoDB
definition: Reduces read latency to microseconds and only serves eventually consistent reads.

meaning: Multi-Region, multi-active tables
definition: Every replica is writable, conflicts are resolved by last-writer-wins; used for DR and access close to users.

meaning: Route 53's DNS routing policies
definition: Simple, Weighted, Latency, Failover, Geolocation, Geoproximity, IP-based and Multivalue answer; combine with health checks to remove failing endpoints.

meaning: An Alias works at the zone apex and is free
definition: A CNAME cannot be set at the root domain; an Alias points to AWS resources such as ELB, CloudFront and S3 websites.

meaning: Only let CloudFront read a private S3 bucket
definition: Keeps the S3 bucket non-public while content is still delivered through the CDN; replaces the old OAI mechanism.

meaning: Running code at CloudFront's edge
definition: CloudFront Functions are lightweight and cheap for header/URL manipulation; Lambda@Edge is more powerful, supports more runtimes and network access.

meaning: A static anycast IP that brings traffic onto the AWS backbone
definition: Supports TCP/UDP, fast failover and no content caching — unlike CloudFront, which is an HTTP caching CDN.

meaning: The trade-off between throughput and ordering/exactly-once
definition: Standard: near-unlimited throughput, at-least-once, best-effort ordering; FIFO: correct ordering per message group, exactly-once processing, lower throughput.

meaning: How long a message is hidden while being processed
definition: Default 30 seconds; after processing the message must be deleted, and once it expires the message reappears and may be processed twice.

meaning: A queue holding messages that failed processing many times
definition: A message exceeding maxReceiveCount moves to the DLQ for investigation instead of looping forever.

meaning: One event delivered to many queues
definition: An SNS topic sends copies to several SQS queues, each consumer processes independently and has a queue's durability.

meaning: An event bus that routes by rule
definition: Receives events from AWS services, SaaS and applications, matches an event pattern and forwards to targets; has a scheduler and a schema registry.

meaning: Latency of initializing a new execution environment
definition: Occurs when Lambda creates a new execution environment; reduce it with provisioned concurrency or SnapStart.

meaning: Two mechanisms for controlling concurrency
definition: Reserved guarantees and limits concurrency for a function; Provisioned keeps environments ready to avoid cold starts (billed).

meaning: The invocation type decides error handling and retries
definition: Synchronous: the caller waits and handles errors itself; Asynchronous: Lambda retries twice by itself and supports DLQ/destinations.

meaning: Lambda automatically polls an event source
definition: Used for SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams — Lambda reads in batches and invokes your function.

meaning: Snapshot the environment for fast startup
definition: Reduces cold starts for supported runtimes by restoring from a snapshot taken after initialization.

meaning: Recovery time and acceptable data loss
definition: RTO is the maximum time the service may be down; RPO is the span of data that can be lost, determining backup/replication frequency.

meaning: Four DR strategies by cost and RTO
definition: Backup & Restore, Pilot Light, Warm Standby, Multi-site Active/Active — the smaller the RTO the higher the cost.

meaning: Continuously replicate servers for fast recovery
definition: Block-level replication from source machines to AWS and launching instances during a disaster.

meaning: A centralized backup service for many AWS services
definition: Schedules, retains and copies backups cross-Region/cross-account with a single policy.

meaning: Fault tolerance within a Region versus DR across Regions
definition: Multi-AZ protects when a datacenter fails; only a cross-Region deployment survives a whole-Region incident.

meaning: EBS volume types
definition: gp3 is the default SSD, io2 is for DBs needing high IOPS, st1/sc1 are HDDs that cannot be boot volumes.

meaning: Attach io2 to several instances
definition: Only io1/io2 within the same AZ; the application must handle concurrent writes itself.

meaning: EFS performance modes
definition: General Purpose vs Max I/O, Bursting/Provisioned/Elastic throughput.

meaning: An HPC file system linked to S3
definition: Very high throughput for HPC and ML, able to load and write back data from S3.

meaning: A physically attached temporary disk
definition: Very high IOPS but data is lost on stop or terminate.

meaning: Query logs in CloudWatch
definition: A query language for filtering and aggregating a log group.

meaning: Collect RAM and disk
definition: EC2 has no RAM metric by default; you need the agent or a custom metric.

meaning: Two kinds of audit events
definition: Management events are on by default; data events such as S3 objects must be enabled separately.

meaning: Evaluate configuration compliance
definition: Records configuration history and automatically fixes violations through SSM.

meaning: Combine several alarms
definition: Reduces noise with AND/OR conditions across alarms.

meaning: ECS's two roles
definition: The task role grants permissions to the application; the execution role lets ECS pull images and write logs.

meaning: Serverless or self-managed nodes
definition: Fargate has no servers to manage but costs more under steady load.

meaning: IAM permissions per pod
definition: Grants a role to each pod instead of the node's role, following least privilege.

meaning: Scaling nodes for EKS
definition: Karpenter creates just-right nodes directly, and faster.

meaning: AWS's container registry
definition: Stores images, scans for vulnerabilities and has lifecycle policies.

meaning: Two API types
definition: REST has many features; HTTP API is cheaper and faster.

meaning: Custom authentication
definition: A Lambda decides whether to allow the request.

meaning: Two workflow types
definition: Standard runs long with exactly-once; Express is short, at-least-once, with high throughput.

meaning: Rate limits and quotas
definition: Limits per stage and per API key.

meaning: Distributing data across shards
definition: Each shard handles 1 MB/s of writes, and ordering is only guaranteed within a shard.

meaning: Dedicated bandwidth per consumer
definition: 2 MB/s per consumer, pushed over HTTP/2.

meaning: Near-real-time delivery
definition: Buffers and then pushes into S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, with no replay.

meaning: Comparing messaging and streaming
definition: Choose by replay, ordering and the number of consumers.

meaning: Reduce the data scanned
definition: You pay by data scanned, so use Parquet and partitions.

meaning: A shared metadata catalog
definition: The schema used by Athena, EMR and Redshift Spectrum.

meaning: Designing MPP tables
definition: A wrong distribution key causes shuffling between nodes.

meaning: Query S3 from Redshift
definition: Extends the warehouse to data in the data lake.

meaning: Data lake permissions
definition: Column- and row-level permissions on the catalog.

meaning: Preview stack changes
definition: Know which resources will be updated or replaced.

meaning: Detect hand-edited configuration
definition: Compares reality with the template.

meaning: Deploy across accounts and Regions
definition: One template deployed across many accounts.

meaning: The levels of abstraction
definition: L1 is close to CloudFormation, L2 has sensible defaults, L3 is a pattern.

meaning: A serverless framework
definition: Extends CloudFormation for Lambda and APIs.

meaning: A maximum-permission guardrail
definition: An SCP limits permissions and does not grant them.

meaning: A multi-account landing zone
definition: Builds a standard environment with guardrails.

meaning: Share resources
definition: Share subnets and Transit Gateway between accounts.

meaning: Separate accounts by workload
definition: A small blast radius and a clear bill.

meaning: Six architectural pillars
definition: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.

meaning: An assessment tool
definition: Lenses for Serverless, SaaS, ML.

meaning: Optimization recommendations
definition: Checks cost, security, performance and service limits.

meaning: The split of responsibility
definition: AWS secures the cloud, the customer secures what is in the cloud.

meaning: Encrypt with a data key
definition: The CMK encrypts the data key, and the data key encrypts the data.

meaning: Rotate secrets automatically
definition: Integrates with RDS and Lambda.

meaning: Threat detection
definition: Analyzes CloudTrail, Flow Logs and DNS.

meaning: Web protection rules
definition: SQLi, XSS and rate-based rules on ALB/CloudFront.

meaning: Authentication vs issuing credentials
definition: The user pool issues JWTs, the identity pool issues AWS credentials.

meaning: Choosing a cache engine
definition: Redis has data structures and HA; Memcached is simple.

meaning: Caching strategies
definition: Lazy loading versus write-through.

meaning: Sharding Redis
definition: Scales capacity and throughput.

meaning: Two kinds of hybrid connectivity
definition: VPN goes over the Internet; DX is a private line.

meaning: Low-downtime DB migration
definition: Change data capture keeps data in sync continuously.

meaning: Move large data with a device
definition: For when bandwidth is not enough.

meaning: Six migration strategies
definition: Rehost, Replatform, Refactor, Repurchase, Retire, Retain.

meaning: AWS's managed CI/CD
definition: A pipeline of stages with a buildspec.

meaning: Zero-downtime deployment
definition: Shifts traffic and rolls back on alarms.

meaning: A shell without SSH
definition: No port 22 and with auditing.

meaning: Deployment strategies
definition: Reduce risk when releasing.

meaning: Publish a private service
definition: No peering or distinct CIDRs needed.

meaning: Observe traffic
definition: Metadata, no payload.

meaning: A managed graph database
definition: Multi-hop relationship queries.

meaning: A time-series database
definition: IoT and metrics.

meaning: Two kinds of commitment
definition: Compute Savings Plans are more flexible than RIs.

meaning: Detailed cost data
definition: Analyzed with Athena.

meaning: Right-sizing recommendations
definition: Based on usage metrics.

meaning: Attribute cost by tag
definition: Must be activated in Billing.

meaning: Distributed tracing
definition: The trace ID travels in a header, with a service map.

meaning: Retry with jitter
definition: Avoids a thundering herd.

meaning: A temporary link
definition: Does not expose credentials.

meaning: Temporary credentials
definition: Grants cross-account permissions.

meaning: Managed GraphQL
definition: Resolvers and subscriptions.

meaning: Immutable backups
definition: WORM protection against deletion.

meaning: WORM for S3
definition: Compliance and governance modes.

meaning: DR strategies
definition: The trade-off between RTO and cost.

meaning: Paths by role
definition: Foundational, Associate, Professional, Specialty.

meaning: Domains and weightings
definition: Secure, resilient, performant, cost-optimized.

meaning: Official learning and practice exams
definition: Practice exams and courses.

meaning: Azure's physical infrastructure
definition: A Region is a set of low-latency datacenters; Availability Zones are locations independent in power, cooling and networking (at least 3 zones in a supporting Region).

meaning: Region pairs for DR
definition: Each Region is paired with another in the same geography; Azure updates them sequentially and prioritizes recovery within a pair.

meaning: Azure's management hierarchy
definition: A Management Group groups subscriptions; a Subscription is the billing and quota boundary; a Resource Group is a logical container; policy and permissions inherit downward.

meaning: Azure's management layer and declarative IaC
definition: ARM handles every management operation and deploys templates/Bicep declaratively.

meaning: Responsibility split by service model
definition: From on-premises to IaaS, PaaS and SaaS, the higher you go the more Azure manages, but data and identity are always the customer's responsibility.

meaning: Identity management service (formerly Azure AD)
definition: Authenticates users and applications with MFA, SSO and passwordless; a tenant can be linked to many subscriptions.

meaning: Resource authorization by role and scope
definition: A role assignment consists of a principal, a role definition and a scope; permissions inherit from the management group down to the resource; Owner, Contributor and Reader are the basic roles.

meaning: Conditional access policy
definition: If conditions (location, device, risk) are met then require MFA or block; needs an Entra ID P1 license.

meaning: Azure-managed identity, no secrets
definition: System-assigned is tied to the resource lifecycle; user-assigned is shared across resources; it replaces storing connection strings in code.

meaning: Just-in-time privileged access
definition: Temporary access with approval and expiry, reducing the risk of permanent Owner access; needs Entra ID P2.

meaning: VM size families by purpose
definition: General purpose (D), compute (F), memory (E), storage (L), GPU (N), HPC (H) — choose by CPU/RAM/IO ratio.

meaning: Spread VMs against hardware failure and maintenance
definition: A fault domain separates power/hardware, an update domain separates maintenance waves within one datacenter (reference SLA 99.95%).

meaning: Identical VMs that autoscale
definition: Autoscale by metric or schedule, combined with a Load Balancer or Application Gateway.

meaning: Two 1–3 year commitments to cut cost
definition: Reserved is tied to a specific VM configuration; Savings Plan commits to an hourly spend and is more flexible.

meaning: Low-cost VMs on spare capacity, can be reclaimed
definition: Up to ~90% cheaper but evicted when capacity is needed; suited to batch, CI and stateless workloads.

meaning: Use existing licenses to cut cost
definition: Applies Windows Server/SQL Server licenses with Software Assurance to Azure resources.

meaning: Storage account redundancy levels
definition: LRS: 3 copies in one datacenter; ZRS: 3 AZs; GRS/GZRS add a second Region; the RA- variants allow reads from the secondary Region.

meaning: Hot, Cool, Cold, Archive by access frequency
definition: Colder tiers are cheap to store but expensive to access and have a minimum retention (30/90/180 days); Archive is offline and must be rehydrated.

meaning: Automatically move tiers or delete blobs
definition: Rules by age or last access time to optimize cost.

meaning: Limited temporary access
definition: Shared Access Signature; a user delegation SAS signed with Entra ID is safer than the account key.

meaning: Protect data from accidental deletion/overwrite
definition: Soft delete and versioning allow recovery; immutable storage (WORM) blocks modification/deletion during the retention period.

meaning: Connect two VNets over the Microsoft backbone
definition: Works in the same or different Regions, is not transitive and needs non-overlapping addresses.

meaning: Allow/deny firewall rules for a subnet or NIC
definition: Rules are processed by priority (lowest number first, 100–4096); default rules allow traffic within the VNet and block inbound Internet.

meaning: Choose load balancing by layer and scope
definition: Load Balancer: L4, per Region; Application Gateway: L7, per Region with WAF; Front Door: global L7 with CDN and WAF.

meaning: Global routing at the DNS layer
definition: Only returns the best endpoint without proxying traffic; failover depends on the DNS TTL.

meaning: Private line versus VPN over the Internet
definition: ExpressRoute does not traverse the Internet and is more stable and faster but expensive; VPN Gateway encrypts traffic over the Internet.

meaning: Access PaaS services via a private IP in the VNet
definition: Attaches a PaaS resource to the VNet through a private IP, avoiding the public Internet.

meaning: Rules about allowed resource configuration
definition: Effects include Deny, Audit, Append, Modify, DeployIfNotExists; grouped into initiatives; distinct from RBAC, which manages user permissions.

meaning: Block accidental deletion or modification
definition: CanNotDelete and ReadOnly, inherited by child resources and applying even to Owners.

meaning: Key-value pairs to classify resources
definition: Not inherited from the resource group; use Azure Policy to enforce tags and support cost reporting.

meaning: Track and alert on cost
definition: Analyze cost by scope and tag, set budgets and alerts; Azure Advisor suggests optimizations.

meaning: Estimate cost and compare with on-premises
definition: The Pricing Calculator estimates Azure service cost; the TCO Calculator compares total cost of ownership with on-premises infrastructure.

meaning: PaaS for running web apps and APIs
definition: The App Service Plan determines resources and price; deployment slots let you swap staging into production with no downtime.

meaning: How Functions connect events and data
definition: A trigger starts the function (HTTP, Timer, Queue, Blob, Event Grid); bindings declaratively read/write data.

meaning: Trade-off between cost, cold start and VNet
definition: Consumption pays per execution and scales to 0 but has cold starts; Premium avoids cold starts and supports VNet.

meaning: Serverless containers versus self-managed Kubernetes
definition: Container Apps hides Kubernetes and scales on events (KEDA); AKS gives full Kubernetes control but takes operational effort.

meaning: Run a single container quickly, no cluster
definition: Billed per second, suited to short tasks or batch.

meaning: The two kinds of Azure Monitor observability data
definition: Metrics are lightweight, near real-time numbers; Logs are more detailed, stored in Log Analytics and queried with KQL.

meaning: Log store queried with Kusto Query Language
definition: Collects logs from resources via diagnostic settings for analysis and alerts.

meaning: APM for applications on Azure Monitor
definition: Tracks requests, dependencies, exceptions and distributed tracing.

meaning: Assess and protect security posture
definition: CSPM with Secure Score and recommendations, plus CWP to protect workloads; supports multicloud.

meaning: Store for secrets, keys and certificates
definition: Accessed via RBAC and managed identity; enable soft delete and purge protection to avoid permanently losing secrets.

meaning: Five consistency levels
definition: Strong, Bounded Staleness, Session, Consistent Prefix, Eventual.

meaning: Partition and RU design
definition: A hot partition causes 429 throttling.

meaning: SQL deployment options
definition: A pool shares resources, MI is SQL Server compatible.

meaning: Multi-Region failover
definition: A group connection string.

meaning: Change stream
definition: Triggers processing after writes.

meaning: Enterprise message broker
definition: Queues, topics, dead-letter, sessions.

meaning: Event distribution
definition: Push to handlers, retry.

meaning: Streaming ingestion
definition: Partitions, consumer groups, Kafka endpoint.

meaning: Comparing the three services
definition: Events vs streams vs commands.

meaning: Azure's IaC
definition: Bicep is more concise and compiles to ARM.

meaning: Preview changes
definition: Avoids surprises when deploying.

meaning: CI/CD
definition: Stages, jobs, environments, approvals.

meaning: Authentication without secrets
definition: The pipeline uses federated tokens.

meaning: Data lake on Blob
definition: POSIX-style ACLs and real directories.

meaning: Data cleansing layers
definition: Bronze is immutable raw data, Silver is cleaned and deduplicated, Gold is modeled for reporting or ML.

meaning: Two SQL modes
definition: Dedicated is MPP, serverless pays per scan.

meaning: ACID on a data lake
definition: Transactions and time travel.

meaning: Unified data platform
definition: OneLake, Lakehouse, Power BI.

meaning: Protection against accidental deletion
definition: Mandatory for production.

meaning: SIEM and SOAR
definition: KQL, rules, playbooks.

meaning: Standard network model
definition: Shared services live in the hub.

meaning: Global hub
definition: Connects many sites and VNets.

meaning: Manage resources outside Azure
definition: Policy and Defender for other servers.

meaning: Two ways to access PaaS
definition: A private IP vs an optimized path.

meaning: Zero-downtime deployment
definition: Slot swap between staging and production.

meaning: Two scaling styles
definition: A bigger instance vs more instances.

meaning: API gateway
definition: Rate-limit and validate-jwt policies.

meaning: Global L7 vs per-Region
definition: Both have WAF.

meaning: Path by role
definition: Fundamentals, Associate, Expert.

meaning: AZ-104 domains
definition: Managing identity, networking, compute, storage, monitoring.

meaning: Composite SLA
definition: Multiply SLAs in series, parallel raises SLA.

meaning: Practice assessment
definition: The official practice test.

meaning: The three basic kinds of machine learning
definition: Supervised has labels (classification, regression); unsupervised has none (clustering); reinforcement learns from environment rewards.

meaning: A model that memorizes or is too simple
definition: Overfitting does well on train but poorly on new data; reduce it with regularization, early stopping and more data.

meaning: Splitting data for correct training and evaluation
definition: Train to learn, validation to select hyperparameters, an independent test to measure final quality.

meaning: Creating and selecting model input features
definition: Transform raw data into features with signal, often deciding model quality.

meaning: Data or patterns that change over time
definition: Degrades the model after deployment; requires monitoring and retraining.

meaning: Ratios derived from the confusion matrix
definition: Precision = TP/(TP+FP), Recall = TP/(TP+FN), F1 is the harmonic mean; choose by which error is more costly.

meaning: Measures class separation across all thresholds
definition: AUC of 0.5 is random, 1.0 is perfect; largely independent of the classification threshold.

meaning: High accuracy but a useless model on imbalanced data
definition: Always predicting the majority class still scores high accuracy; use Precision/Recall/F1/AUC instead.

meaning: Two error measures for regression
definition: MAE is the easy-to-read mean absolute error; RMSE heavily penalizes large errors and shares the target's unit.

meaning: Evaluating text generated by models
definition: ROUGE for summarization, BLEU for machine translation, BERTScore measures embedding-based semantic similarity.

meaning: An LLM's processing unit and context limit
definition: A token is a text fragment; the context window is the total tokens (prompt + answer) the model processes at once; cost is billed per token.

meaning: Parameters that tune output randomness
definition: A low temperature gives stable results, a high one gives creativity; top-p/top-k limit the candidate token set when sampling.

meaning: Techniques for writing effective prompts
definition: Zero-shot, few-shot with examples, chain-of-thought asking for step-by-step reasoning, system prompt setting role and rules.

meaning: Vectors representing the semantics of text
definition: Text with similar meaning has nearby vectors; the foundation of semantic search and RAG.

meaning: A model confidently fabricating information
definition: Reduce it with RAG, requiring source citations, low temperature and verification of important outputs.

meaning: An attack that injects instructions into a prompt
definition: Untrusted content can hijack model behavior; separate instructions from data and limit agent permissions.

meaning: Retrieve documents then put them in the prompt for the LLM
definition: Solves stale knowledge, private data and hallucination without retraining the model.

meaning: Store for embeddings and similarity search
definition: Finds the top-k nearest vectors by cosine similarity; for example OpenSearch, Aurora pgvector, Azure AI Search.

meaning: How documents are split affects retrieval quality
definition: Small chunks are precise but lack context; large chunks have enough context but add noise and cost tokens.

meaning: Managed RAG on AWS
definition: Automatically chunks, embeds, stores vectors, retrieves and generates answers with citations.

meaning: Full-text, vector and hybrid search service
definition: Indexes documents, enriches them with AI (skillsets), commonly used as the RAG store for Azure OpenAI.

meaning: Choose between updating knowledge and changing model behavior
definition: RAG suits private data that changes often; fine-tuning suits a stable specialized style or task.

meaning: Microsoft's six Responsible AI principles
definition: Fairness, Reliability & Safety, Privacy & Security, Inclusiveness, Transparency, Accountability.

meaning: AWS's Responsible AI dimensions
definition: Fairness, explainability, privacy & security, safety, controllability, veracity & robustness, governance, transparency.

meaning: Detect bias and explain predictions
definition: Measures bias in data and models and provides explainability for each prediction.

meaning: Filter content, denied topics and PII for LLMs
definition: Applied to inputs and outputs: denied topics, word filters, PII masking, grounding checks.

meaning: Harmful content moderation service
definition: Detects hate, sexual, violence and self-harm content in text and images.

meaning: Put humans in the loop to review AI results
definition: Routes low-confidence predictions to human reviewers.

meaning: Access many foundation models through one API
definition: A managed serverless service; customer data is not used to train the foundation models.

meaning: A unified conversational API for many models
definition: Supports multi-turn conversation, streaming and tool use with the same interface.

meaning: Buy committed capacity for a model
definition: Required for customized models; suited to stable high load compared with on-demand.

meaning: Agents that plan and call actions
definition: The LLM breaks down tasks, calls action groups (Lambda/API) and Knowledge Bases to reach the goal.

meaning: Ways to customize foundation models
definition: Fine-tuning uses labeled data; continued pre-training uses unlabeled data to add domain knowledge.

meaning: Four ways to deploy a model
definition: Real-time, serverless, asynchronous and batch transform — choose by latency, payload and load.

meaning: A feature store shared by training and inference
definition: Stores features both online and offline to avoid skew between training and prediction.

meaning: Monitors drift and quality after deployment
definition: Compares real data with a baseline built from training data to alert on drift.

meaning: Automatically tries many algorithms and hyperparameters
definition: Delivers good models with little code and supports explanations.

meaning: Pre-trained models and ready-made templates
definition: Quickly deploy or fine-tune popular models.

meaning: Automate the training and deployment workflow
definition: CI/CD for ML with a Model Registry managing versions and approvals.

meaning: Extracting document structure versus recognizing images
definition: Textract reads text, tables and forms in scanned documents; Rekognition recognizes objects, faces and text in images/video.

meaning: AWS's ready-made NLP service
definition: Analyzes sentiment, entities, key phrases, language and detects PII in text.

meaning: Speech to text and the reverse
definition: Transcribe is speech-to-text; Polly is text-to-speech.

meaning: Build conversational chatbots and voice bots
definition: Uses Alexa-like technology to understand intents and fill slots in conversation.

meaning: Enterprise search powered by ML
definition: Semantic search across many internal document sources.

meaning: Three layers: AI services, ML platforms and infrastructure
definition: AI services are ready-made APIs; Bedrock/SageMaker build and customize; the bottom layer is GPU, Trainium and Inferentia infrastructure.

meaning: Two kinds of AI services resource
definition: Multi-service uses one endpoint and key for many services; single-service separates endpoint, key and cost per service.

meaning: Extract data from invoices, receipts and forms
definition: Formerly Form Recognizer; uses prebuilt or custom models to get text, tables and key-values.

meaning: Azure's NLP capabilities
definition: Sentiment analysis, entity recognition, summarization, CLU for conversational intent understanding and question answering.

meaning: Two-way speech and text conversion
definition: Speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech translation.

meaning: AI workload types in the AI-900 exam
definition: Computer vision, NLP, document intelligence, knowledge mining and generative AI.

meaning: Model deployment types
definition: Standard is billed per token; Provisioned (PTU) reserves capacity with stable latency; there are also Global, Data Zone and Batch.

meaning: Token quota and rate-limit error handling
definition: Quota is in tokens-per-minute; exceeding it returns HTTP 429, handled by retry with exponential backoff or raising the quota.

meaning: RAG over internal documents with citations
definition: Connects Azure AI Search so the model answers from the organization's data.

meaning: Content filters for prompts and responses
definition: Filters hate, sexual, violence, self-harm; configurable, with added jailbreak and groundedness protection.

meaning: Build and manage AI agents on Azure
definition: Foundry is the platform bringing together models, agents, evaluation and safety; the branding may change.

meaning: The model calls external functions or tools
definition: The model returns a structured function call for the application to execute and feed the result back.

meaning: Manage model versions
definition: Stages, approval, reproducibility.

meaning: Two kinds of data drift
definition: The input changes vs the relationship changes.

meaning: Feature consistency
definition: Define once for offline and online.

meaning: Deploying models safely
definition: Compare the new model with the old.

meaning: Data leaking during training
definition: Using future information.

meaning: The three-step SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK handshake that creates a connection
definition: Costs 1 RTT before data can be sent; the reason to reuse connections instead of constantly opening new ones.

meaning: The mechanism TCP uses to avoid congesting the network
definition: Starts with slow start, grows the send window gradually and cuts sharply on packet loss; distinct from flow control, which protects the receiver.

meaning: The trade-off between reliability and latency
definition: TCP guarantees ordering and delivery; UDP is connectionless and fast, the basis of DNS, video and QUIC.

meaning: Resolving names via a resolver and caching by TTL
definition: The resolver asks root, TLD, authoritative; results are cached by TTL so an IP change has propagation delay.

meaning: Running out of ports when opening/closing too many short connections
definition: A closed connection lingers in TIME_WAIT for a while; rapid opens exhaust ephemeral ports — solved with connection pooling.

meaning: Reference latency table for RAM, disk and network
definition: For quick estimates: within a datacenter about 0.5 ms, intercontinental about 100–200 ms.

meaning: Three HTTP generations that differ in multiplexing and HOL blocking
definition: HTTP/2 multiplexes many streams over one TCP connection; HTTP/3 runs on QUIC (UDP) to remove head-of-line blocking at the TCP layer.

meaning: A TLS handshake needing only 1 RTT
definition: Negotiates the cipher, exchanges keys and authenticates the certificate faster than TLS 1.2 (2 RTTs).

meaning: The UDP-based protocol underlying HTTP/3
definition: Independent streams, integrated TLS 1.3, 0/1-RTT support and network changes without dropping the connection.

meaning: Caching and revalidation at the HTTP layer
definition: Cache-Control sets how long to keep; ETag with If-None-Match lets the server return 304 Not Modified.

meaning: Telling the confusable error codes apart
definition: 401 is unauthenticated, 403 is not permitted; 502 the upstream returned an error, 504 the upstream timed out.

meaning: The difference in address space and cost
definition: A process has its own address space and good isolation; threads share the heap, are lighter but need synchronization.

meaning: The cost of switching context between threads
definition: Saving/restoring state and cooling the CPU cache; too many threads lowers performance.

meaning: Memory management and the consequences of running out of RAM
definition: The page table maps virtual memory; low RAM means very slow swap, and exhausting it makes the OOM killer kill processes.

meaning: The foundation of container isolation and resource limits
definition: Namespaces isolate the system view; cgroups limit CPU/RAM and can throttle CPU.

meaning: Choose the thread pool size by workload type
definition: CPU-bound should be about the number of cores; I/O-bound can be much larger because most of the time is spent waiting.

meaning: The limit on a process's open files/sockets
definition: The Too many open files error is usually caused by leaked connections or a ulimit that is too low.

meaning: A bug where check-then-act is not atomic
definition: The result depends on the threads' execution order, for example two threads both see stock equal to 1 and both decrement it.

meaning: The four conditions that cause deadlock
definition: Mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption and circular wait; break one condition (usually the lock order) to avoid it.

meaning: An atomic update without a lock
definition: Compare the current value and only then write; retry on failure — the basis of lock-free and optimistic concurrency.

meaning: Guarantee that other threads see written data
definition: Without synchronization, CPU caches and reordering make other threads see stale values; you need volatile, locks or atomics.

meaning: Two strategies for handling contention
definition: Pessimistic locks before modifying; optimistic proceeds, then checks for conflict (version/CAS) and retries.

meaning: Avoid shared state by passing messages
definition: Each actor owns its own state and communicates only via messages, so no locks are needed.

meaning: Scale up and scale out
definition: Vertical is simple but has a ceiling and is a SPOF; horizontal is nearly unlimited but requires stateless services.

meaning: Push state out to scale horizontally
definition: Any request can go to any instance; state lives in a shared DB or cache.

meaning: Quickly estimate QPS, capacity and bandwidth
definition: For example 1 million requests per day is roughly 12 QPS; peak is usually 2–5 times the average.

meaning: The relation between concurrency, arrival rate and processing time
definition: L = λ × W; used to compute the threads or connections needed for a given load.

meaning: Tail latency matters more than the average
definition: With fan-out across many services, each service's p99 determines the overall experience.

meaning: How to read and compute availability
definition: 99.9% is roughly 8.76 hours of downtime per year; chaining services in series multiplies the probabilities.

meaning: How cost grows with input size
definition: Describes the order of growth, not absolute time; distinguishes average from worst case.

meaning: Hash tables and handling collisions
definition: Lookup is O(1) on average, O(n) worst case; user-controlled keys can cause hash flooding.

meaning: Efficiently getting the priority element
definition: Get min or max in O(1), insert and delete in O(log n); used for schedulers and top-K.

meaning: Ordering by dependency
definition: Used for build order, task dependencies and prerequisite graphs.

meaning: The average cost of an operation
definition: Appending to a dynamic array is O(1) amortized even though it occasionally reallocates.

meaning: Two memory regions and their lifetimes
definition: The stack follows function calls automatically, fast and limited; the heap holds objects that outlive a single call.

meaning: Generational collection
definition: Most objects die young, so the young generation is collected often and cheaply, the old generation rarely and expensively.

meaning: GC pauses
definition: Low-latency GCs reduce pause time by working concurrently with the application.

meaning: A leak from holding references
definition: Objects remain referenced unnecessarily, such as an unbounded cache or listeners that are never removed.

meaning: Memory safety without GC
definition: Ownership is checked at compile time to prevent use-after-free and data races.

meaning: Two ways a thread handles waiting for I/O
definition: Blocking hangs the thread until data arrives; non-blocking returns immediately so it can do other work.

meaning: The kernel reports which sockets are ready
definition: One thread watches tens of thousands of connections, solving the C10K problem.

meaning: The event loop
definition: The foundation of Node.js and Nginx: wait for events and then call the matching handler.

meaning: Lightweight threads managed by the runtime
definition: Let you write simple blocking code that still scales to millions of tasks.

meaning: Controlling producer and consumer speed
definition: Pauses or limits when the consumer is slow to avoid swelling in-memory queues.

meaning: A quick-check command sequence
definition: uptime, vmstat, iostat, free, top and ss give an overview in one minute.

meaning: Tracing syscalls, files, sockets and packets
definition: A toolset to see what a process is doing and which connections are open.

meaning: Why load is high while CPU is idle
definition: Load counts processes waiting on I/O too, so high load with low CPU usually means an I/O bottleneck.

meaning: Diagnose disk I/O bottlenecks
definition: Look at await and %util to see whether the disk is saturated.

meaning: Low-intrusion observation of the Linux kernel
definition: Run small programs in the kernel to trace syscalls and events with low overhead.

meaning: Store absolute instants, display by time zone
definition: Store UTC or epoch and convert to the user's time zone only for display.

meaning: Use zone names instead of offsets
definition: Offsets change with DST and each country's rules, so use names like Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh.

meaning: The duration clock and the wall clock
definition: Monotonic only moves forward and is used to measure timeouts; the wall clock can jump when NTP adjusts it.

meaning: Standard time formats for APIs
definition: For example 2026-11-21T09:30:00Z, unambiguous unlike 03/04/2026.

meaning: Wrong assumptions about time
definition: A list of false beliefs such as every day having 24 hours or clocks always moving forward.

meaning: Two kinds of workload and their design consequences
definition: OLTP is short row-based transactions; OLAP is large scans and column-based aggregation.

meaning: Dimensional model for analytics
definition: A fact table holds measures surrounded by dimension tables holding context.

meaning: Keeping dimension change history
definition: Add a new row with valid_from and valid_to so past reports do not change.

meaning: Why column stores are fast for analytics
definition: Read only the needed columns, compress well and run vectorized execution; weaker at single-row updates.

meaning: Start modeling from the grain
definition: The grain defines what one fact row represents; a wrong grain doubles totals.

meaning: Substitute keys in dimensions
definition: Artificial keys independent of business keys, required for SCD.

meaning: Processing finite and infinite data
definition: Batch gives high throughput with minute-to-hour latency; stream gives low latency but is more complex to operate.

meaning: Two notions of time in streams
definition: Event time is when the event happened; business figures should be computed by event time.

meaning: Closing windows and handling late data
definition: A watermark estimates that all data up to time T has been seen; windows include tumbling, sliding and session.

meaning: Two architectures combining batch and stream
definition: Lambda runs two paths in parallel and duplicates logic; Kappa is stream-only and reprocesses by replay.

meaning: Stream processing in small batches
definition: A middle point between batch and stream with a few seconds of latency and a simpler model.

meaning: Exactly-once semantics and practical limits
definition: Only correct within a framework and sinks that support transactions or are idempotent.

meaning: Data model and how consumers split work
definition: Ordering only within a partition; each partition belongs to one consumer in a group, so maximum parallelism equals the partition count.

meaning: Write durability configuration
definition: acks=all with min.insync.replicas and replication factor 3 so no data is lost when one broker fails.

meaning: Deduplication and read-process-write handling
definition: An idempotent producer removes duplicates on retry; transactions give exactly-once within Kafka.

meaning: Keep the latest value per key
definition: Used for changelogs and state tables; different from time-based retention.

meaning: Monitoring lag and handling rebalances
definition: Rising lag means a slow consumer; overly long processing causes continuous rebalancing.

meaning: Kafka's new metadata architecture
definition: Kafka manages metadata itself with Raft, removing the ZooKeeper dependency.

meaning: Transform before or after loading into the target
definition: ELT loads raw data into the warehouse then transforms it with SQL, using the warehouse's compute power.

meaning: Airflow's scheduling and rerun concepts
definition: A DAG consists of tasks and dependencies; each run covers one data interval; backfill reruns past intervals.

meaning: Pipelines whose reruns do not duplicate data
definition: Overwrite a partition or MERGE by key and use the logical date instead of now().

meaning: SQL transforms, testing and incremental loads
definition: A model is versioned SQL; tests check not_null, unique and referential relationships.

meaning: Load only the changed data
definition: Use an updated_at column or CDC to load incrementally instead of reloading everything.

meaning: Comparing orchestration tools
definition: They differ in task versus asset model, developer experience and operations.

meaning: Three distributed storage architectures
definition: A lake is cheap and flexible; a warehouse is fast and managed; a lakehouse adds an ACID table layer to a lake.

meaning: An ACID table layer on object storage
definition: Adds transactions, schema evolution and time travel to Parquet files.

meaning: A columnar format that speeds up queries
definition: Reads only the needed columns and skips data blocks that fail the condition thanks to min/max statistics.

meaning: The small files problem and its remedy
definition: Too many small files slow queries; compaction merges them into files of a sensible size.

meaning: Scale storage and compute independently
definition: Data lives in object storage; compute engines are switched on/off and scaled separately.

meaning: Snapshots and the exactly-once guarantee
definition: Periodically snapshot state and source offsets to recover without losing or duplicating effects.

meaning: Taking a consistent snapshot on a data stream
definition: Barriers inserted into the stream let every operator snapshot its state at the same logical point.

meaning: Closing windows when a source emits no data
definition: One idle partition stalls the watermark; configure idleness.

meaning: Keep large state on disk
definition: RocksDB lets state exceed memory and supports incremental checkpoints.

meaning: A transactional sink to achieve exactly-once
definition: Prepare and commit the sink in step with checkpoints so external effects happen only once.

meaning: Choosing a stream processing engine
definition: Kafka Streams is an embedded library, Flink is true streaming with large state, Spark is micro-batch.
